core_claims: CoreCoin is a decentralized Layer-1 digital asset
CoreCoin operates on a Proof-of-Stake (PoS) blockchain
CoreCoin supports smart contracts
CoreCoin supports decentralized applications
CoreCoin has an average block time of ~5 seconds
The maximum supply of CoreCoin is 2,000,000,000 CORE
Transactions are secured through cryptographic signatures
The network relies on distributed validator participation
CoreCoin's market value is highly volatile
CoreCoin's market value is influenced by liquidity, market sentiment, and macroeconomic conditions
Price discovery occurs through decentralized market mechanisms
Trading is subject to 24/7 global activity
CoreCoin can be stored on hardware wallets
CoreCoin can be stored on mobile wallets
CoreCoin can be stored on desktop clients
Compatibility varies by software
Users must securely store their private keys
Private keys cannot be recovered if lost
The self-custody model places responsibility on the user
No third-party key recovery is available
CoreCoin supports smart contracts
CoreCoin supports decentralized application integration
CoreCoin is compatible with PoS-compatible virtual machines
CoreCoin enables the development and execution of programmable smart contracts
CoreCoin employs a community-driven, on-chain governance model
Protocol updates require community or validator approval
Governance participation is dependent on wallet integration and token ownership
On-chain governance votes are publicly recorded
CoreCoin is not natively cross-chain compatible unless explicitly specified
Interoperability with other blockchains is not a built-in feature of CoreCoin's architecture
Staking CoreCoin requires locking tokens for defined protocol periods
The minimum stake is a protocol-defined threshold
The lockup period is governance-defined
Rewards depend on network participation and validator performance
Unstaking early may reduce a user's historical reward rate
disclaimers: Cryptocurrency investments involve risk and are highly volatile
Do not invest funds you cannot afford to lose
CoreCoin is not backed by the FDIC or any government entity
Past performance is not indicative of future results
Loss of private keys leads to permanent loss of funds
Digital assets may be vulnerable to hacking or protocol exploits
Market conditions can change rapidly and unpredictably
Regulatory changes may affect accessibility or legality
